audit.whatIsWrong: Three rows are wrong, and one of them contradicts its own text: win[2] reads Ziggs while whys[2] literally says 'call it Skill rather than yours'. Levels 4-5 read Skill while whys[3] says his bomb kit out-zones you. Level 6 reads Ziggs while whys[4] calls it 'your genuine ownership window'. Packet chart: Skill, Ziggs, Riven.
audit.why: 47.97% over 813 games — the shape is right (his lane early, Riven's one window at 6) but the chart put the window in the wrong row and gave him a stage his own text hands to skill.
audit.corrected: Level 3 -> Skill, Levels 4-5 -> Ziggs, Level 6 -> Riven, as three matched full/content pairs, with ratings 5/10, 3/10 and 6/10.

audit.why: Four spikes present and ordered: Lvl 2-3 Satchel Charge, Lvl 6 Blade of the Exile, 1st item Eclipse, late full-AP Ziggs. The Level 6 spike is now the only Riven row on the chart, which matches.

audit.whatIsWrong: whys[4] and mid call Wind Slash an 'execute', and mid tells the player to 'burn your second R cast' as though the R had two damage casts. Riven's R grants AD and range plus one use of Wind Slash. Separately, Short Fuse being an auto-attack reset is never mentioned, and Hexplosive Minefield's flat 16s cooldown is never given.
audit.why: Short Fuse is what makes his step-up chip hurt, and its cooldown shortens every time he casts an ability — the wind-up is the tell the page never gave.
audit.corrected: Wind Slash: one ranged projectile per Blade of the Exile. Satchel Charge: 20/18/16/14/12s, knocks both of you away, percent-health damage. Hexplosive Minefield: flat 16s, slow. Short Fuse: passive auto reset, cooldown reduced by his casts.

audit.why: Satchel Charge is correctly the tracked cooldown across both layers; its 12-20s range is now stated in whys[4].

edits.before: Levels 4-5 his bomb kit out-zones you before your items are online; approach paths through Minefield are slow and predictable, letting him land Q chains while you are still in approach animation.
edits.after: Levels 4-5 his bomb kit out-zones you before your items land; Minefield (flat 16s) slows every approach, and Short Fuse resets his auto — the wind-up is your cue to step back, not the cast.

edits.before: Blade of the Exile's extended range and Wind Slash execute force Ziggs to respect your Level 6 burst — this is your genuine ownership window if Satchel Charge is down when you run the all-in.
edits.after: Blade of the Exile's extended range and your one ranged Wind Slash force Ziggs to respect Level 6 — this is your ownership window if Satchel Charge (12-20s) is down when you commit.

edits.before: Levels 4-5 Ziggs zones you hard — his Hexplosive Minefield (E) denies your approach angles and his bombs out-range your dashes, so these two levels belong to him unless he overextends. Save your action for Level 6: Blade of the Exile extends your reach and makes Wind Slash a genuine execute threat, which finally forces Ziggs to respect your presence rather than just spam and step back. When Satchel Charge is down at 6, E in, Q chain into W stun, and burn your second R cast — half-HP Ziggs does not survive a clean Wind Slash.
edits.after: Levels 4-5 Ziggs zones you hard — Hexplosive Minefield (E, a flat 16s at every rank) denies your approach angles and his bombs out-range your dashes, so these two levels belong to him unless he overextends. Save your action for Level 6: Blade of the Exile extends your reach and arms one ranged Wind Slash, which finally forces Ziggs to respect your presence rather than just spam and step back. When Satchel Charge is down at 6, E in, Q chain into W stun, then spend Wind Slash — a chunked Ziggs does not survive that sequence.
